Add duplicate attribute tracking for CSP nonce validation (#695)

* Add duplicate attribute tracking for CSP nonce validation.

Implements detection and propagation of duplicate attributes through
the tokenizer, tree builder, and TreeSink interface to support CSP
(Content Security Policy) nonce validation.

This enables html5ever consumers (e.g., Servo) to properly implement
step 3 of the CSP "is element nonceable" algorithm by checking the
`ElementFlags.had_duplicate_attrs` field during nonce validation.

Reference:
 - https://www.w3.org/TR/CSP/#is-element-nonceable
 - https://github.com/servo/servo/commit/4821bc0ab01e1ed0bb27e86c2df545019bd3856a

publisher_trust.limits: Every added record is one historical UTC day [start,end) for one named package and exact verified publisher; future releases and unrelated packages are not trusted. These are heuristic maintainer/release trust decisions for safe-to-deploy, not exemptions, independent human audits or assertions of absent vulnerabilities.

agent_audits.name: dirs
agent_audits.analysis: Read both manifests and all five complete Rust source modules, including the embedded smoke test and Linux/macOS/Windows/wasm implementations. This crate is safe Rust with no build script, own FFI, filesystem writes, subprocesses or network. Each public method delegates to a selected backend; XDG base-directory environment values must be absolute before acceptance, otherwise a fixed home-relative fallback is joined. macOS uses fixed Library/user-directory suffixes, Windows calls named dirs-sys Known Folder wrappers and wasm returns None. Returned environment/OS-controlled paths are locations, not an authorization/confinement proof; HOME and XDG user-dir results can contain parent components or arbitrary paths and must not be used to grant capabilities. User-directory lookups delegate local-file parsing to dirs-sys, whose input validation and memory safety remain separately unaudited; no claim that those calls cannot panic on malformed local configuration. Runtime smoke test was not run because it prints real local paths. Dependencies retain their own audit requirement.

agent_audits.name: cesu8
agent_audits.analysis: Read the sole published manifest (no Cargo.toml.orig in this historical archive) and both complete source modules, including the embedded tests and width table. No dependencies, build script, native code, I/O or OS authority. For decoding, the fast path uses standard UTF-8 validation; the fallback accepts only ASCII, valid non-overlong 2/3-byte sequences and a validated high/low surrogate pair, whose arithmetic stays in U+10000..U+10FFFF before UTF-8 construction. These cases justify String::from_utf8_unchecked. Encoding starts from valid Rust str, advances only by its scalar width and checks bounds before the unchecked 4-byte subslice conversion. The allocation capacity expression underestimates typical output and may over-allocate/grow; Vec remains bounds checked and overflow/OOM/resource limits are caller concerns. Important semantic limit: valid UTF-8 is returned by the decoder fast path even when it includes literal NUL in Java mode or native 4-byte sequences. Therefore these decoders are converters, not strict canonical CESU-8/modified-UTF-8 validators or security filters. No serious production exploit identified under that documented review boundary.

agent_audits.name: android_system_properties
agent_audits.analysis: Read both manifests, the complete single library source and time_zone example. Reviewed every unsafe block, Send/Sync impl, function-pointer ABI, callback and Drop. Only fixed libc.so and fixed system-property symbol names are dynamically loaded on Android; the handle outlives all calls and is closed once on exclusive Drop. Bionic property access is thread-safe, function fields are immutable and callback output is a stack-owned Option<String> valid for the synchronous read_callback call; invalid UTF-8 produces None. The old getter reserves PROP_VALUE_MAX=92 bytes, relies on the documented Android API bound including its terminator, checks the returned length before set_len and converts initialized bytes with checked UTF-8. CString rejects interior NUL; no name is executed or used as a pathname. Non-Android construction has no functions/handle and returns None. Allocation OOM aborts rather than unwinding a Rust panic through C; arbitrary replacement libc implementations are outside the OS trust model. This is intentional access to possibly identifying OS property data, not authorization to collect or transmit it; NymWrap lane/sandbox/egress policy remains separate. No build script, native archive, network or subprocess. Android runtime and cross-platform builds were not tested on this Windows reviewer host; source review relies on the Bionic ABI contract and independently vetted libc.

agent_audits.name: tower-service
agent_audits.analysis: Read both manifests and the complete src/lib.rs, including examples and the readiness/backpressure contract. The crate only declares Service with Future/Response/Error associated types and forwards calls through &mut S and Box<S>. It forbids unsafe code, has no production dependencies, build script, generated/native code, I/O, sockets or environment access. The readiness requirement can cause panics in implementations; it does not confer memory safety or authorize network access. Documentation logging/network examples are not executed by the library. Implementors, futures and downstream services are separate audit obligations.

agent_audits.name: tower-layer
agent_audits.analysis: Read both manifests and all five complete production modules, including the unit test and documentation examples. Identity returns its input, LayerFn invokes a caller-supplied Fn, Stack composes inner then outer, and tuple implementations compose the listed layers from right to left for lengths zero through sixteen. There is no evaluation of input text; closures are caller-provided compiled Rust. Borrowing and ownership remain safe Rust, unsafe code is forbidden and there are no production dependencies, build script, I/O, OS or network operations. Debug formatting exposes layer Debug values/type names and must not be treated as a secret logger. Layer implementations and code shown only in examples are not certified.

agent_audits.name: new_debug_unreachable
agent_audits.analysis: Read both manifests, complete src/lib.rs, example and integration test. The no_std macro panics with unreachable! in debug and expands to core::hint::unreachable_unchecked in release. It deliberately does not introduce its own unsafe block, so safe caller code cannot use the release intrinsic without an unsafe context. Production use requires a proof the branch is unreachable; untrusted input must never be the sole reason for that assertion. The publicly re-exported intrinsic remains unsafe. The empty macro arm uses an unqualified recursive macro name: possible caller shadowing/compilation issues are not privilege escalation because caller macros are already compiled code. No dependencies, build script, FFI, I/O or ambient authority. Debug and release behavior were considered separately.

agent_audits.name: static_vcruntime
agent_audits.analysis: Read both manifests and complete src/lib.rs. No dependencies, build script of its own, unsafe, FFI, subprocess, filesystem or network operations. metabuild reads only CARGO_CFG_TARGET_ENV, requires the documented Cargo build-script environment, returns unless it equals msvc and prints eleven fixed linker arguments. Neither environment value nor external text is interpolated into arguments. The arguments deliberately suppress conflicting CRT variants and choose static startup/VCRuntime with dynamic UCRT; deployment must respect CRT ownership/link compatibility, especially external C/C++ libraries. This is a build helper under the trusted Cargo/MSVC toolchain assumption, not a runtime sanitizer or arbitrary-environment API.

agent_audits.name: endi
agent_audits.analysis: Read both manifests and all three complete source modules including numeric unit tests. Endian methods use fixed-size primitive from/to_le/be_bytes conversions and checked slices; too-short caller buffers panic as documented and cannot overrun memory. All unsigned/signed 8/16/32/64/128-bit and f32/f64 sizes match their primitives. std ReadBytes uses initialized fixed stack arrays and read_exact, returning I/O errors before conversion; WriteBytes uses write_all and propagates partial-write errors. Streams are supplied by the caller: the crate opens no file, socket or OS resource. No unsafe, native code, dependencies or build script. NaN payloads are byte conversions, not arithmetic or semantic validation; users must validate their own protocol values.

agent_audits.name: secrecy
agent_audits.analysis: Read both manifests and the entire single production module, including optional serde implementations. Safe no_std code owns a Box<S>, exposes values only through explicit borrowing traits, invokes Zeroize on Drop and redacts Debug without formatting the value. Clone is opt-in via CloneableSecret for general boxed secrets, with deliberate slice/string copying implementations. SerializableSecret gates general serialization; deserialization can allocate and creates temporary secret copies. init_with/try_init_with clone a local and then zeroize that local; a panicking user Clone or compiler-created copies are not guaranteed erased. Drop cannot protect abort/forget, prior caller copies, swap or intermediates from deserialization; no mlock or complete memory-erasure guarantee is claimed. into_boxed_str/slice may reallocate before the wrapper takes ownership. These documented limits require downstream secret-lifetime discipline. The library forbids unsafe and has no build script, FFI, OS, filesystem, network or subprocess access. Zeroize/Serde implementation safety and downstream use remain separate audits.

agent_audits.name: idna_adapter
agent_audits.analysis: Read both manifests and the entire src/lib.rs. A no_std typed adapter delegates UTS46 normalization/validation and Unicode scalar property lookup to ICU4X with borrowed static data. Joining/Bidi masks shift only documented ICU4C numeric enum values and GeneralCategory discriminants; the API provides no attacker-selected shift count. Reviewed all composed bidi masks, mark categories, intersections and transparent/LTR/number predicates. Iterators preserve caller lifetime and borrow, no unsafe or raw memory operations. No own parsing allocation, build script, FFI, file/network/process/environment operations. Unicode data correctness, ICU4X and the higher-level IDNA policy remain separate obligations; this adapter is not the complete domain-name validator. Optional compiled_data only adds immutable constructors.

agent_audits.name: dtoa-short
agent_audits.analysis: Read both manifests and complete src/lib.rs (the only Rust source). Also inspected the locked dtoa 1.0.11 Buffer definition, format_finite contract and sealed Float interface to check the local unsafe preconditions; this is not a separate audit of dtoa. dtoa returns ASCII backed by its 25-byte Buffer; scratch is size_of<Buffer>+1, so copying the returned bytes at offset one stays within a distinct initialized allocation. Float is sealed to f32/f64 and precision is private/fixed at 6/15, preventing hostile implementations or size arithmetic. restrict_prec uses checked indexing, a leading carry slot, finite bounded loops, ASCII digit edits and forward copies when the exponent moves left; these preserve UTF-8 for the release unchecked conversion. Writer errors propagate and the caller owns the fmt::Write destination; no file/socket is opened. No build script, OS authority or FFI. Nonfinite values have dtoa format_finite's unspecified numeric representation and negative zero may normalize to zero; not a roundtrip/financial serializer. Dependencies remain separately vetted.
